thesis: Development-stage miner advancing the Stibnite Gold Project in Idaho — one of the largest undeveloped U.S. gold deposits (6M+ oz gold) plus ~148M lbs antimony, the only domestic mined antimony source amid China's export bans. The biggest overhang is gone: the U.S. EXIM Bank board unanimously finalized a $2.9B senior secured loan under 'Make More in America', leaving Stibnite effectively fully financed. Construction is advancing after an Idaho federal court rejected efforts to halt critical-path work and the Burntlog Route commenced; initial production is targeted for late 2029. Despite full financing the stock sits near a 52-week low on a gold pullback and dilution/'sell-the-news', shifting the thesis from financing risk to construction execution, commodity price, and dilution risk.

drivers: EXIM $2.9B loan drawdowns proceed smoothly, keeping the project fully funded to first pour
Gold price recovers and holds above $3,200/oz, lifting project NAV
Antimony prices stay elevated on Chinese export bans; defense offtake agreements signed
Construction stays on schedule with first production in H2 2029
Additional strategic partnerships (defense, battery, government) announced

risks: Significant construction cost overruns (industry average 20-40%) on a first-time mine build
Gold and antimony price declines impair project economics
Further equity dilution required despite the EXIM debt facility
Permitting/environmental opposition or litigation delays critical-path construction
Prolonged 'sell-the-news' and gold-price weakness keep the equity oversold

base_case.assumptions: EXIM $2.9B facility draws down on schedule; gold ~$3,000/oz; construction advances with only minor delays; first production H2 2029; modest further equity dilution; antimony offtake agreements signed with defense contractors.

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 results and construction/financing progress update
EXIM $2.9B loan drawdown / financial close milestones
Stibnite construction milestones — Burntlog Route, mill, tailings facility
Antimony offtake agreements with defense contractors

key_risks: Execution risk: first mine development with no operating history; cost overruns common (20-40%)
Commodity price risk: gold and antimony price volatility affects project economics and valuation
Dilution risk: further equity raises possible despite the EXIM debt facility
Regulatory/environmental risk: ongoing permitting scrutiny and opposition/litigation in Idaho
Sentiment/technical risk: shares near 52-week low, oversold, pressured by gold pullback and 'sell-the-news'
